previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. He had been discharged recently after treatment for right leg cellulitis. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation, likely due to medication noncompliance, with associated cardiorenal syndrome and elevated creatinine. He was treated with intravenous furosemide twice daily for seven days, resulting in improved dyspnea, resolution of pulmonary edema, and return of creatinine to baseline. His atrial fibrillation remained rate-controlled, though digoxin was briefly held and warfarin dose increased due to subtherapeutic INR. He was discharged home with home health services on oral furosemide, warfarin, and other baseline medications, with instructions to monitor weight, continue compression stockings, and follow up for INR testing.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Dyspnea and chest pain.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors from ___ - ___.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral chest radiographs demonstrate large bilateral
pleural effusions, greater on the right, mildly increased from ___. 
Mild pulmonary vascular congestion is also evident.  The cardiac silhouette is
not well visualized.  Atherosclerotic calcifications are noted in the aortic
arch.  There is no pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  Dysphagia.

COMPARISON:  None available.

BARIUM ESOPHAGRAM:  Upon initial standing views of the esophagus with sips of
thick barium, note was made of proximal escape of the primary peristaltic
wave, although the contrast was seen to pass through the esophagus without
evidence of significant holdup.  There was no hiatal hernia seen.  

In the right anterior oblique position, the patient was given several sips of
thin barium, and likewise, there was proximal escape of the primary
peristaltic wave with tertiary contractions in the mid esophagus; however, the
bolus of contrast eventually passed into the stomach via secondary
peristalsis.  No stricture are area focal stenosis is identified.  No focal
mass lesion is seen.  

The patient was given a 13-mm barium tablet which was momentarily held up at
the level of the aortic arch, which is calcified, but eventually passed with
subsequent sips of water.  Limited views of the stomach are unremarkable.  No
free reflux is identified.

IMPRESSION:  

Esophageal dysmotility and tertiary contractions with no evidence of focal
stenosis or mass lesion.
